### CANDIDATE DETAIL
#### 1. seizures, benign familial neonatal, 1  —  Tier 1 — Definitive / Highly Plausible  (fitness 0.783)
**Link type:** shared causal gene (HGNC:6296)

**Proposed mechanism:** KCNQ2 (HGNC:6296) —DISRUPTS→ Voltage-gated potassium channel activity (GO:0005249); Voltage-gated potassium channel activity (GO:0005249) —LEADS_TO→ Seizure (HP:0001250); Voltage-gated potassium channel activity (GO:0005249) —LEADS_TO→ Neonatal seizures (HP:0007150). Pathogenic variants in KCNQ2 lead to haploinsufficiency, disrupting normal voltage-gated potassium channel activity. This disruption underlies the common phenotype of seizures (HP:0001250), and specifically neonatal seizures (HP:0007150) in the context of benign familial neonatal seizures.

**How to falsify it:** Identification of pathogenic variants in KCNQ2 that cause loss-of-function in both diseases, but with distinct downstream effects on neuronal excitability that cannot be explained by haploinsufficiency of the same channel function. _(variant: rs74315379)_

**Why it matters:** Understanding the shared KCNQ2 channel dysfunction in both conditions could lead to therapeutic strategies targeting potassium channel activity to manage seizures in both rare epilepsy syndromes.

#### 2. developmental and epileptic encephalopathy 6B  —  Tier 3 — Moderate / Emerging  (fitness 0.436)
**Link type:** shared pathway (Reactome:R-HSA-445095)

**Proposed mechanism:** KCNQ2 (HGNC:6378) —DISRUPTS→ Neuronal excitability (GO:0007224); SCN1A (HGNC:10593) —DISRUPTS→ Neuronal excitability (GO:0007224); Neuronal excitability (GO:0007224) —LEADS_TO→ Seizure (HP:0001250); Neuronal excitability (GO:0007224) —LEADS_TO→ Developmental delay (HP:0001263). Mutations in KCNQ2 (associated with MONDO:0013387) and SCN1A (associated with developmental and epileptic encephalopathy 6B) both disrupt the normal regulation of neuronal excitability, leading to overlapping phenotypes such as seizures and developmental delay.

**How to falsify it:** Identification of individuals with pathogenic variants in KCNQ2 or SCN1A presenting with phenotypes entirely distinct from seizures and developmental delay, or conversely, individuals with these phenotypes lacking any pathogenic variants in these genes. _(variant: Presence of common variants (AF > 0.01) in KCNQ2 or SCN1A in the general population that are not associated with either disease.)_

**Why it matters:** Understanding the shared mechanism of disrupted neuronal excitability provides a common target for therapeutic interventions aimed at managing seizures and improving developmental outcomes in patients with both MONDO:0013387 and developmental and epileptic encephalopathy 6B.

Mutations in SCN1A (causing MONDO:0011461) and KCNQ2 (causing MONDO:0013387) both disrupt the normal regulation of neuronal excitability, a shared pathway leading to distinct but related epilepsy phenotypes.

**How to falsify it:** Discovery of a pathogenic variant in SCN1A or KCNQ2 with a population frequency >1% in gnomAD. _(variant: Pathogenic variants in SCN1A or KCNQ2 with >1% allele frequency in gnomAD.)_

**Why it matters:** Understanding the shared mechanism of disrupted neuronal excitability due to ion channel dysfunction in these two epilepsy syndromes could lead to the development of targeted therapies that modulate neuronal activity, potentially benefiting patients with either condition.

#### 4. neurodevelopmental disorder with neuromuscular and skeletal abnormalities  —  Tier 3 — Moderate / Emerging  (fitness 0.423)
**Link type:** shared pathway (Reactome:R-HSA-445095)

**Proposed mechanism:** KCNQ2 (HGNC:6279) —DISRUPTS→ Potassium channel activity (GO:0005400); Potassium channel activity (GO:0005400) —LEADS_TO→ Seizures (HP:0001250); NRCAM (HGNC:7759) —DISRUPTS→ Neuronal cell adhesion (GO:0007107); Neuronal cell adhesion (GO:0007107) —LEADS_TO→ Skeletal abnormalities (HP:0000707); Neuronal cell adhesion (GO:0007107) —LEADS_TO→ Neuromuscular abnormalities (HP:0002412). Disruption of KCNQ2 leads to impaired potassium channel activity, resulting in seizures. Disruption of NRCAM impairs neuronal cell adhesion, leading to neuromuscular and skeletal abnormalities. The convergence is on the broad cellular processes of ion channel regulation and cell adhesion, critical for neuronal development and function.

**How to falsify it:** If genetic studies show that pathogenic variants in KCNQ2 do not segregate with MONDO:0013387, or if pathogenic variants in NRCAM do not segregate with neurodevelopmental disorder with neuromuscular and skeletal abnormalities, this hypothesis would be falsified. Additionally, if individuals with mutations in KCNQ2 do not exhibit phenotypes related to neuronal cell adhesion disruption, or if individuals with mutations in NRCAM do not exhibit phenotypes related to ion channel dysfunction, it would weaken the proposed overlap.

**Why it matters:** Understanding the shared molecular underpinnings of these distinct rare diseases can facilitate the identification of common therapeutic targets or strategies for neurodevelopmental disorders. For instance, modulating pathways involved in ion channel function or cell adhesion could potentially benefit patients with either condition.

**Link type:** shared pathway (Reactome:R-HSA-445095)

**Proposed mechanism:** Loss-of-function variant in CACNA1A (HGNC:1675) —DISRUPTS→ CACNA1A (HGNC:1675); CACNA1A (HGNC:1675) —DECREASES→ Neuronal calcium influx (GO:0007234); Neuronal calcium influx (GO:0007234) —LEADS_TO→ Seizure (HP:0001250); Gain-of-function variant in CACNA1A (HGNC:1675) —DISRUPTS→ CACNA1A (HGNC:1675); CACNA1A (HGNC:1675) —INCREASES→ Neuronal excitability (GO:0009955); Neuronal excitability (GO:0009955) —LEADS_TO→ Migraine with aura (HP:0011425). Loss-of-function variants in CACNA1A (leading to reduced neuronal calcium influx and seizures in MONDO:0013387) and gain-of-function variants in CACNA1A (leading to increased neuronal excitability and migraine in familial hemiplegic migraine) converge on the shared biological process of regulating neuronal excitability via calcium channel activity.

**How to falsify it:** If variants in CACNA1A associated with MONDO:0013387 are exclusively loss-of-function and variants associated with familial hemiplegic migraine are exclusively gain-of-function, and no other shared molecular mechanism is identified, this hypothesis would be falsified. _(variant: A pathogenic loss-of-function variant for MONDO:0013387 with a gnomAD allele frequency > 0.01% or a pathogenic gain-of-function variant for familial hemiplegic migraine with a gnomAD allele frequency > 0.01% would challenge causality.)_

**Why it matters:** Understanding the shared role of CACNA1A in both epilepsy and migraine could lead to the development of therapies targeting calcium channel function, potentially benefiting patients with either condition.
